**This is a pre-release for testing:** `pip install nmdc-schema==11.25.0rc3`. Built with linkml and linkml-runtime 1.12.1. These notes cover everything since v11.24.1, not only since rc2.

## Summary

v11.25.0 removes the Biosample slot `collection_time_inc`, adds classes and slots for stable isotope probing (SIP) metagenomics, adds EMSL analysis types, imports its MIxS slots from MIxS v7.0.1 instead of v6.3.0, supports Python 3.14, and is built with linkml and linkml-runtime 1.12.1. It is a minor release even though it removes a slot. Removals in v11 have been released as minor versions, which does not match the rule in MAINTAINERS.md; that is being discussed in https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/2876.

For consumers that read the generated JSON Schema, the linkml 1.12 build changes four things: id patterns now have the form `^(?:(nmdc):...)$` (for example `^(?:(nmdc):sty-([0-9][a-z]{0,6}[0-9])-([A-Za-z0-9]{1,}))$`), `type` also accepts the full class URI, optional enum- and class-ranged slots accept `null`, and slot examples appear in the JSON Schema. nmdc-runtime's ID minter reads only patterns that start `^(nmdc):`, so nmdc-runtime must take https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-runtime/pull/1659 (Read LinkML 1.12 wrapped id patterns in the minter's typecodes(); head 1171f379, which expects the `^(?:(nmdc):` form) in the same change that moves its pin to 11.25.0. What changes for each consumer and what each has to do is on this docs page: https://microbiomedata.github.io/nmdc-schema/release-11.25.0/

## Migration

`migrator_from_11_24_1_to_11_25_0` changes no data. It fails if any `biosample_set` document still has `collection_time_inc`. No other change can invalidate existing data: a SchemaView diff from v11.24.1 found `collection_time_inc` was the only removal, the MIxS v7.0.1 import leaves the JSON Schema unchanged apart from descriptions, titles and examples, and on 2026-10-15 none of 1,902,502 patterned values or 51,744,347 functional_annotation_agg documents in production failed the new patterns.

## Schema changes

- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3396 (Add new classes for SIP metagenomics data modeling), by @aclum. Adds the classes `IsotopeLabelingProcess`, `DensityGradientFractionationProcess`, `IsotopologAddition` and `IsotopologComposition`, 16 slots, and the enums `IsotopeEnum`, `IsotopologApproachEnum` and `IsotopologLabelEnum`. Adds permissible values to `ChemicalEntityEnum`, `ProtocolCategoryEnum` (`stable_isotope_probing`), `ProtocolForEnum` and `UnitEnum` (`g/mL`).
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3499 (Record which slot each method slot describes), by @turbomam. Adds a `method_for` annotation to 21 method slots, for example `ph_meth` gets `method_for: ph`.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3483 (Add interpolated: true to three id structured patterns), by @turbomam. Fixes the `id` patterns of `ChromatographicSeparationProcess`, `Manifest` and `MixingProcess`, which linkml 1.12 would otherwise leave as literal `{id_nmdc_prefix}` text. The expanded patterns are unchanged under linkml 1.11.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3508 (Remove the yq lines that create an empty `internal_standard` slot), by @turbomam. Removes an unused stub slot. It was introduced after v11.24.1, so v11.24.1 users see no change.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3471 (Add EMSL specific analysis types to support user submissions), by @bmeluch. Adds 10 permissible values to `AnalysisTypeEnum`, matching the analysis options in the EMSL submission templates, for example `proteomics`, `isotope profiling` and `imaging - xray`. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/2629 and https://github.com/microbiomedata/issues/issues/1137.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3524 (Give each schema module its own copy of the settings its patterns use), by @turbomam. linkml-runtime 1.12 fills in a `structured_pattern` only from the `settings:` of the module that defines it (https://github.com/linkml/linkml/issues/4135), so each module now carries a copy of the settings it uses, kept in sync from `nmdc.yaml` by `src/scripts/sync_module_settings.py`. Patterns resolve the same under 1.11.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3519 (Keep five descriptions to the definition and move the rest to comments), by @turbomam. Text only. Three of the changed descriptions are `MetadataBadgeEnum` values, which the Data Portal shows as badge tooltips.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3542 (Fix 16 spelling errors in schema descriptions and docs), by @turbomam. Text only.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3544 (Keep the base id slot's MAG example out of every class's id), by @turbomam. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3540 (Under linkml 1.12, every class's id example is the base slot's MAG id, which fails 40 class patterns).
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3545 (Give each class its own id example, using production ids), by @turbomam.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3501 (Import MIxS v7.0.1), by @turbomam. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3480 (Import MIxS v7.0.1 (we still import v6.3.0)). All 504 imported MIxS slots now come from MIxS v7.0.1; 492 of them moved from v6.3.0. NMDC keeps the name `estimated_size` (MIxS renamed it `estimated_genome_size`, recorded as a structured alias) and keeps `env_medium` single-valued (MIxS v7.0.0 made it multivalued), so no migrator is needed: JSON Schema built from main and from the branch on 2026-10-14 was identical apart from descriptions, titles and examples. `salinity_meth`, which MIxS dropped after v6.1.1, now uses the default `nmdc:` URI and no longer maps to MIXS:0000341, which returns 404. Approved by @mslarae13. Adopting `estimated_genome_size` (https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3526) or a multivalued `env_medium` (https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3527) later would need a migrator.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3549 (Leave anchoring of structured patterns to linkml), by @turbomam. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3539. linkml 1.12 adds its own `^(?:...)$` around structured patterns, so rc2 shipped doubled anchors such as `^(?:^(nmdc):sty-...$)$`. 107 structured patterns drop their own `^` and `$`, so all 40 NMDC id patterns now read `^(?:(nmdc):...)$`. What matches is unchanged. Three of 522 patterns stay doubled: `salinity_meth` (kept for submission-schema, which resolves patterns with linkml-runtime 1.9.5) and the imported MIxS slots `cult_root_med` and `genetic_mod`.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3555 (Correct the MIxS release that dropped host_family_relation and soil_text_measure), by @turbomam. Text only: the notes on those two slots now say MIxS dropped them in v6.2.0, not v6.2.2.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3516 (Record structured alias origins in source, not contexts), by @turbomam. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3454. 14 structured aliases move their origin from `contexts` to `source`, and a new test requires a `source` on every structured alias. Alias metadata only.

## Removals and deprecations

- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3470 (Finalize deprecation of `collection_time_inc`), by @JamesTessmer. Removes `collection_time_inc` from `Biosample` and records it in `deprecated.yaml`. Use `collection_time` for the harvested sample's collection time.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3474 (Remove `collection_time_inc` rows from NCBI mapping and OLS4 alignment assets), by @turbomam.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3478 (Record elements removed during v11 in deprecated.yaml, with a catalog of all removals), by @turbomam. Adds `make retired-element-catalog` and `assets/schema_element_history/retired_elements.tsv`.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3479 (Scan for retired element names in files nothing checks), by @turbomam.

## Migrator

- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3495 (Add a migrator check that fails on `collection_time_inc`), by @turbomam. `migrator_from_11_24_1_to_11_25_0` changes no data. It raises if any `biosample_set` document still has `collection_time_inc`, because there is no automatic place to move the value.

## Python package and dependencies

- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3511 (Prepare `get_typecode_for_future_ids` for LinkML v1.12 and add associated test), by @kheal. With linkml-runtime 1.12, `get_typecode_for_future_ids` returned `None` for several classes, which breaks ID minting. nmdc-schema allows `linkml-runtime>=1.9.0,<2.0.0`, and 1.12.0 has been on PyPI since 2026-10-08 (1.12.1 since 2026-10-13), so a pip install of v11.24.1 can already get the broken combination. This release fixes it for both 1.11 and 1.12.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3532 (Hold our lock at linkml-runtime 1.11 until nmdc-runtime can read wrapped id patterns), by @turbomam. Puts the repo's own lock back at linkml-runtime 1.11.1 after the Dependabot update in https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3530 moved it to 1.12.1. A release built under 1.12 would ship id patterns wrapped as `^(?:...)$`, which nmdc-runtime's ID minter can't read until https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-runtime/pull/1659 is deployed. What consumers can install is unchanged: the package still allows `linkml-runtime>=1.9.0,<2.0.0`. https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3529 later moved the lock to 1.12.1 for the release.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3528 (Move dependency management from Poetry to uv), by @turbomam. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/2761 (Consider migrating from Poetry to uv for dependency management) and https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3411 (Document installing Poetry on Python 3.13 so poetry run stops searching for an interpreter). This changes how nmdc-schema is developed and built, not how it is installed.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3529 (Lock linkml 1.12.1 by overriding pronto's chardet cap in uv.lock), by @turbomam. The release is built with linkml and linkml-runtime 1.12.1. The published dependency ranges stay `linkml>=1.9.0,<2.0.0` and `linkml-runtime>=1.9.0,<2.0.0`, so consumers keep the linkml they lock. The override is in our `uv.lock` only (https://github.com/althonos/pronto/issues/247).
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3536 (Remove the requests warning suppression from the Makefile), by @turbomam. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/2875 (Suppress or resolve RequestsDependencyWarning from urllib3/chardet version mismatch) and https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/2889 (Remove RequestsDependencyWarning suppression when requests fixes version check).
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3488 (Allow Python 3.14 and test it in CI), by @turbomam. `requires-python` goes from `>=3.10,<3.14` to `>=3.10,<3.15`. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3487.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3486 (Allow version 3.x of the `deprecated` dependency), by @turbomam.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3503 (Raise the pymdown-extensions cap to <13.0.0), by @turbomam.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3502 (Pin the three owlgen options whose defaults will change), by @turbomam.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3472 (Bump the python-dependencies group with 4 updates), by Dependabot.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3530 (Bump the python-dependencies group with 5 updates), by Dependabot. Its linkml-runtime 1.12.1 lock change was reverted by https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3532.

## Tests and CI

- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3525 (Test the schema against linkml 1.12's structured pattern handling), by @turbomam. It merged into the branch of https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3524, not into main directly.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3512 (Add doctests for LinkML 1.12 wrapped id patterns), by @turbomam. The doctests are in `nmdc_schema/id_helpers.py`, which ships in the package.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3531 (Bump the github-actions group with 3 updates), by Dependabot.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3534 (Bump astral-sh/setup-uv from 9.0.0 to 10.3.0 in the github-actions group), by Dependabot.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3515 (Test the installed wheel weekly with the newest allowed dependencies), by @turbomam.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3504 (Test that new NMDC multivalued slots have plural names), by @turbomam.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3462 (Pin poetry 2.5.1 everywhere and test that the pins agree), by @turbomam.

## Docs and repository tooling

- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3431 (Document schema consumers and compatibility rollout), by @turbomam.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3496 (Let the OLS4 embeddings search run on named classes, slots or enums), by @turbomam.

## Highlights

This is a pre-release for testing. It adds stable isotope probing (SIP) modeling, removes `collection_time_inc` from `Biosample`, and is the first release built and published with uv instead of Poetry.

- **SIP modeling:** new classes `IsotopeLabelingProcess`, `DensityGradientFractionationProcess`, `IsotopologAddition` and `IsotopologComposition`, and new enums `IsotopeEnum`, `IsotopologApproachEnum` and `IsotopologLabelEnum`.
- **`collection_time_inc` removed from `Biosample`.** The 11.24.1 to 11.25.0 migrator changes nothing; it stops with an error if any Biosample still has the slot, so a person can decide where the value goes.
- **EMSL analysis types:** ten new `AnalysisTypeEnum` values, for example `proteomics` and `imaging - electron`.
- **Python 3.14:** `requires-python` is now `>=3.10,<3.15`.
- **Build:** dependencies are locked in `uv.lock`, and the package is built with hatchling and `uv-dynamic-versioning`. The published dependency ranges are unchanged.

**Migration:** no data transformation. The migrator only checks for `collection_time_inc`.

**Known issue:** a rule-required single-valued slot accepts an explicit `null` in the JSON Schema, which affects the new `IsotopologAddition`: https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3424

**For consumers:** pre-releases are not installed unless asked for. Test with `nmdc-schema==11.25.0rc1`.

**Version note:** this release is tagged `v11.25` and published to PyPI as `11.25`, not `11.25.0`. pip and uv treat `nmdc-schema==11.25.0` as this release. The notes below call it 11.25.0.

## Summary

v11.25.0 removes the Biosample slot `collection_time_inc`, adds classes and slots for stable isotope probing (SIP) metagenomics, adds EMSL analysis types, imports its MIxS slots from MIxS v7.0.1 instead of v6.3.0, supports Python 3.14, and is built with linkml and linkml-runtime 1.12.1. It is a minor release even though it removes a slot. Removals in v11 have been released as minor versions, which does not match the rule in MAINTAINERS.md; that is being discussed in https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/2876.

For consumers that read the generated JSON Schema, the linkml 1.12 build changes four things: id patterns now have the form `^(?:(nmdc):...)$` (for example `^(?:(nmdc):sty-([0-9][a-z]{0,6}[0-9])-([A-Za-z0-9]{1,}))$`), `type` also accepts the full class URI, optional enum- and class-ranged slots accept `null`, and slot examples appear in the JSON Schema. nmdc-runtime's ID minter reads only patterns that start `^(nmdc):`, so nmdc-runtime must take https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-runtime/pull/1659 (Read LinkML 1.12 wrapped id patterns in the minter's typecodes(); head 1171f379, which expects the `^(?:(nmdc):` form) in the same change that moves its pin to 11.25.0. What changes for each consumer and what each has to do is on this docs page: https://microbiomedata.github.io/nmdc-schema/release-11.25.0/

## What consumers need to do

- **nmdc-runtime:** merge https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-runtime/pull/1659 in the same change that moves the pin to 11.25.0. Without it the minter finds no typecodes.
- **nmdc-server:** nothing for nmdc-schema 11.25.0. Keep `nmdc-submission-schema==11.24.0` until https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-server/issues/2401 is fixed.
- **submission-schema:** move the dev pin, rebuild and release nmdc-submission-schema 11.25.0.
- **nmdc_mass_spectrometry_metadata_generation and nmdc-mass-spec-automation:** move their pins to 11.25.0, which fixes their linkml 1.12 failures.
- **nmdc-lakehouse and nmdc-lakehouse-schema:** accept 11.25.0 as a source version (https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-lakehouse/pull/396, https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-lakehouse-schema/pull/28).
- **Anything that reads pattern strings from the JSON Schema** must accept the `^(?:...)$` wrapping. `nmdc_schema.get_typecode_for_future_ids` already does.

Known gaps shipping in 11.25.0: `type` also accepts the full class URI (https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3537), and optional enum- and class-ranged slots accept `null` (https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3424).

## Migration

`migrator_from_11_24_1_to_11_25_0` changes no data. It fails if any `biosample_set` document still has `collection_time_inc`. No other change can invalidate existing data: a SchemaView diff from v11.24.1 found `collection_time_inc` was the only removal, the MIxS v7.0.1 import leaves the JSON Schema unchanged apart from descriptions, titles and examples, and on 2026-10-15 none of 1,902,502 patterned values or 51,744,347 functional_annotation_agg documents in production failed the new patterns.

## Schema changes

- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3396 (Add new classes for SIP metagenomics data modeling), by @aclum. Adds the classes `IsotopeLabelingProcess`, `DensityGradientFractionationProcess`, `IsotopologAddition` and `IsotopologComposition`, 16 slots, and the enums `IsotopeEnum`, `IsotopologApproachEnum` and `IsotopologLabelEnum`. Adds permissible values to `ChemicalEntityEnum`, `ProtocolCategoryEnum` (`stable_isotope_probing`), `ProtocolForEnum` and `UnitEnum` (`g/mL`).
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3499 (Record which slot each method slot describes), by @turbomam. Adds a `method_for` annotation to 21 method slots, for example `ph_meth` gets `method_for: ph`.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3483 (Add interpolated: true to three id structured patterns), by @turbomam. Fixes the `id` patterns of `ChromatographicSeparationProcess`, `Manifest` and `MixingProcess`, which linkml 1.12 would otherwise leave as literal `{id_nmdc_prefix}` text. The expanded patterns are unchanged under linkml 1.11.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3508 (Remove the yq lines that create an empty `internal_standard` slot), by @turbomam. Removes an unused stub slot. It was introduced after v11.24.1, so v11.24.1 users see no change.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3471 (Add EMSL specific analysis types to support user submissions), by @bmeluch. Adds 10 permissible values to `AnalysisTypeEnum`, matching the analysis options in the EMSL submission templates, for example `proteomics`, `isotope profiling` and `imaging - xray`. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/2629 and https://github.com/microbiomedata/issues/issues/1137.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3524 (Give each schema module its own copy of the settings its patterns use), by @turbomam. linkml-runtime 1.12 fills in a `structured_pattern` only from the `settings:` of the module that defines it (https://github.com/linkml/linkml/issues/4135), so each module now carries a copy of the settings it uses, kept in sync from `nmdc.yaml` by `src/scripts/sync_module_settings.py`. Patterns resolve the same under 1.11.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3519 (Keep five descriptions to the definition and move the rest to comments), by @turbomam. Text only. Three of the changed descriptions are `MetadataBadgeEnum` values, which the Data Portal shows as badge tooltips.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3542 (Fix 16 spelling errors in schema descriptions and docs), by @turbomam. Text only.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3544 (Keep the base id slot's MAG example out of every class's id), by @turbomam. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3540 (Under linkml 1.12, every class's id example is the base slot's MAG id, which fails 40 class patterns).
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3545 (Give each class its own id example, using production ids), by @turbomam.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3501 (Import MIxS v7.0.1), by @turbomam. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3480 (Import MIxS v7.0.1 (we still import v6.3.0)). All 504 imported MIxS slots now come from MIxS v7.0.1; 492 of them moved from v6.3.0. NMDC keeps the name `estimated_size` (MIxS renamed it `estimated_genome_size`, recorded as a structured alias) and keeps `env_medium` single-valued (MIxS v7.0.0 made it multivalued), so no migrator is needed: JSON Schema built from main and from the branch on 2026-10-14 was identical apart from descriptions, titles and examples. `salinity_meth`, which MIxS dropped after v6.1.1, now uses the default `nmdc:` URI and no longer maps to MIXS:0000341, which returns 404. Approved by @mslarae13. Adopting `estimated_genome_size` (https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3526) or a multivalued `env_medium` (https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3527) later would need a migrator.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3549 (Leave anchoring of structured patterns to linkml), by @turbomam. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3539. linkml 1.12 adds its own `^(?:...)$` around structured patterns, so rc2 shipped doubled anchors such as `^(?:^(nmdc):sty-...$)$`. 107 structured patterns drop their own `^` and `$`, so all 40 NMDC id patterns now read `^(?:(nmdc):...)$`. What matches is unchanged. Three of 522 patterns stay doubled: `salinity_meth` (kept for submission-schema, which resolves patterns with linkml-runtime 1.9.5) and the imported MIxS slots `cult_root_med` and `genetic_mod`.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3555 (Correct the MIxS release that dropped host_family_relation and soil_text_measure), by @turbomam. Text only: the notes on those two slots now say MIxS dropped them in v6.2.0, not v6.2.2.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3516 (Record structured alias origins in source, not contexts), by @turbomam. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3454. 14 structured aliases move their origin from `contexts` to `source`, and a new test requires a `source` on every structured alias. Alias metadata only.

## Removals and deprecations

- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3470 (Finalize deprecation of `collection_time_inc`), by @JamesTessmer. Removes `collection_time_inc` from `Biosample` and records it in `deprecated.yaml`. Use `collection_time` for the harvested sample's collection time.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3474 (Remove `collection_time_inc` rows from NCBI mapping and OLS4 alignment assets), by @turbomam.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3478 (Record elements removed during v11 in deprecated.yaml, with a catalog of all removals), by @turbomam. Adds `make retired-element-catalog` and `assets/schema_element_history/retired_elements.tsv`.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3479 (Scan for retired element names in files nothing checks), by @turbomam.

## Migrator

- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3495 (Add a migrator check that fails on `collection_time_inc`), by @turbomam. `migrator_from_11_24_1_to_11_25_0` changes no data. It raises if any `biosample_set` document still has `collection_time_inc`, because there is no automatic place to move the value.

## Python package and dependencies

- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3511 (Prepare `get_typecode_for_future_ids` for LinkML v1.12 and add associated test), by @kheal. With linkml-runtime 1.12, `get_typecode_for_future_ids` returned `None` for several classes, which breaks ID minting. nmdc-schema allows `linkml-runtime>=1.9.0,<2.0.0`, and 1.12.0 has been on PyPI since 2026-10-08 (1.12.1 since 2026-10-13), so a pip install of v11.24.1 can already get the broken combination. This release fixes it for both 1.11 and 1.12.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3532 (Hold our lock at linkml-runtime 1.11 until nmdc-runtime can read wrapped id patterns), by @turbomam. Puts the repo's own lock back at linkml-runtime 1.11.1 after the Dependabot update in https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3530 moved it to 1.12.1. A release built under 1.12 would ship id patterns wrapped as `^(?:...)$`, which nmdc-runtime's ID minter can't read until https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-runtime/pull/1659 is deployed. What consumers can install is unchanged: the package still allows `linkml-runtime>=1.9.0,<2.0.0`. https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3529 later moved the lock to 1.12.1 for the release.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3528 (Move dependency management from Poetry to uv), by @turbomam. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/2761 (Consider migrating from Poetry to uv for dependency management) and https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3411 (Document installing Poetry on Python 3.13 so poetry run stops searching for an interpreter). This changes how nmdc-schema is developed and built, not how it is installed.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3529 (Lock linkml 1.12.1 by overriding pronto's chardet cap in uv.lock), by @turbomam. The release is built with linkml and linkml-runtime 1.12.1. The published dependency ranges stay `linkml>=1.9.0,<2.0.0` and `linkml-runtime>=1.9.0,<2.0.0`, so consumers keep the linkml they lock. The override is in our `uv.lock` only (https://github.com/althonos/pronto/issues/247).
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3536 (Remove the requests warning suppression from the Makefile), by @turbomam. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/2875 (Suppress or resolve RequestsDependencyWarning from urllib3/chardet version mismatch) and https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/2889 (Remove RequestsDependencyWarning suppression when requests fixes version check).
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3488 (Allow Python 3.14 and test it in CI), by @turbomam. `requires-python` goes from `>=3.10,<3.14` to `>=3.10,<3.15`. Closes https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/issues/3487.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3486 (Allow version 3.x of the `deprecated` dependency), by @turbomam.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3503 (Raise the pymdown-extensions cap to <13.0.0), by @turbomam.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3502 (Pin the three owlgen options whose defaults will change), by @turbomam.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3472 (Bump the python-dependencies group with 4 updates), by Dependabot.
- https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3530 (Bump the python-dependencies group with 5 updates), by Dependabot. Its linkml-runtime 1.12.1 lock change was reverted by https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-schema/pull/3532.

## Tests and CI

# Lobster AI 1.2.1

## Installation

```bash
uv pip install "lobster-ai[full]==1.2.1"
```

[PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/lobster-ai/1.2.1/) · [Documentation](https://docs.omics-os.com)

## Single-cell QC and filtering
- QC tools report the computed pre-filter medians, 95th percentiles (linear interpolation), the number of cells above each threshold, and the parameters that were actually applied.
- The `filter_and_normalize` tool no longer applies a ribosomal filter by default. Set `max_ribo_percent` to request one. The service/SDK default (50%) is unchanged.
- Normalization requests that Lobster does not support are refused before the data is changed or stored.

## Clustering
- `cluster_cells` uses the `n_neighbors` and `n_pcs` you request. When they are not set, the defaults stay 15 and 30, and any automatic adjustment is reported.
- Without `use_rep`, `cluster_cells` runs the standard pipeline as before. With `use_rep`, it reuses a representation that is already in the dataset, for example `X_pca` or `X_scvi`, instead of rerunning the upstream steps.
- If you name a representation that is not in the dataset, or one that does not hold one row of finite numbers per cell, clustering stops with a message that says so. Previously it silently ran the full pipeline instead. Explicit values that cannot be honored are refused in the same way.
- Notebook replay follows the clustering branch that actually ran.

## Marker genes
- Marker reports keep the original ranking and the specificity-filtered list separate, and label ranked, filtered and FDR-significant genes distinctly.
- Genes with |log2FC| ≥ 10 or a non-finite statistic are flagged in the report, not removed. The statistics themselves are unchanged.
- A dataset can be saved after marker ranking, including after later annotation. Previously, empty gene-name slots in the ranking could stop the save.

## Saves
- Save failures that were previously reported as saved now report `Not saved:`.
- A MuData save of a backed modality now checks its backup location before loading any data.

## Reading files
- Compressed CSV, TSV and TXT matrices loaded in single-cell mode are checked across the complete matrix to orient cells as observations and genes as variables. This applies to direct file loading, not to GEO candidate selection. Some GEO text matrices are still refused; see Known limitations.
- Integral matrices within 2^24 are stored exactly as float32; larger integral values are refused. Fractional matrices use float32 precision, which can differ from the source. The loader does not establish raw-count provenance.
- This compressed single-cell route reports fixed refusals when content, completeness or orientation cannot be established, or when its storage limits are exceeded.

## Notebook export
- Exports show the client session ID, or `null` when it is unknown or ambiguous, instead of the provenance namespace. The namespace is recorded under its own key, `provenance_namespace`, in the export record and the notebook metadata.
- **Export hashes change.** The input of `provenance.sha256` now includes the session ID and the provenance namespace, so a notebook exported with 1.2.1 has a different hash from the same session exported with 1.2.0. The hash still covers only the session ID, the namespace and the activity and entity counts, not the content of the provenance record.
- The export summary no longer describes the provenance JSON as an audit trail for regulatory compliance.

## Exports outside the workspace
- Lobster's export tools (DE tables, annotation mappings, ML exports, scVI model files, pathway CSVs) refuse a target outside the session workspace, unless you listed the folder in `LOBSTER_EXPORT_ROOTS`. You set it yourself in the environment. List existing absolute folders, separated by `:` (`;` on Windows); relative, missing or non-folder entries are ignored. Lobster reads the setting when it loads its export policy, so restart Lobster after changing it. The refusal names the setting, not the path.
- This applies to the export tools. Save paths that you give as absolute paths are unchanged, and custom code is not limited by this setting.
- Auto-save skips a dataset whose target is outside the workspace and reports it as `Not saved:`. The other datasets are still saved.
- Dataset names must be one plain name: no `/`, `\`, control characters, `.` or `..`, and at most 200 characters.
- DE result names encode `%`, `/`, `\` and control characters in group labels (percent-encoding), so different labels give different names.

## Installation and dependencies
- `lobster-ai[full]` now includes `lobster-metadata`, so the metadata assistant is available after a `[full]` install.
- The HDF refusal test no longer requires PyTables. The HDF read policy is unchanged.

## Known limitations
### Omics-OS Cloud sign-in
- `lobster cloud login` in the Python package does not work with the current Omics-OS Cloud sign-in. Use the npm CLI `@omicsos/lobster` to sign in; the Python package then uses that saved sign-in. This is planned for a later release.

### Data import
- The GEO download does not yet pick the expression matrix of series that ship only a gene-by-cell text file, for example GSE109564. This is planned for a later release. Workaround: read the downloaded file yourself with pandas (`pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t", index_col=0)`, which gives genes × cells), build an AnnData with cells as observations (`anndata.AnnData(X=scipy.sparse.csr_matrix(df.T.values.astype("float32")), obs=pd.DataFrame(index=df.columns), var=pd.DataFrame(index=df.index))`), write it with `write_h5ad`, and load the `.h5ad` file in Lobster. We checked this for GSE109564 with Lobster's file-loading service (4,487 cells × 20,477 genes).
- Some compressed GEO text matrices, for example the GSE109564 matrix, are refused when a few row labels are not recognized as gene names (such as `HGNC:12345`, `Y_RNA` or `Metazoa_SRP`), even if the other labels are. Setting `transpose` explicitly does not change this. Loading these files is planned for a later release.
- If saving a required GEO import fails (for example, disk full), that queue entry cannot be retried in the same session, and a partial file may remain in the workspace. Remove the partial file from the workspace and start a new session.

### Metadata validation
- After metadata has been fetched and cached, `validate_dataset_metadata` can return "Already Validated" without running the metadata validation service. This cached-status reply does not confirm that the requested validation checks ran. This is planned for a later release.

### Differential expression results
- DE results with "/" in a comparison group label can become unavailable through their saved result pointer after an H5AD save and reload. If two result keys differ only by "/" versus "__" (for example `de_results_A/B_vs_C` and `de_results_A__B_vs_C`), saving collapses them to one key and only one result is kept. Use group labels without "/" before running DE; renaming a dataset or export file afterwards does not repair results that already exist, so rerun them from the original input with "/"-free labels. This is planned for a later release.
- In cluster-versus-rest marker summaries, a "Top 10 Downregulated" heading can appear above genes with a positive fold change. The reported statistics are not affected. This is planned for a later release.

### Notebook export
- After you resume a saved session, a pipeline exported with `/pipeline export` can contain some steps twice, so the exported notebook may repeat filtering or normalization. Check the notebook before you run it again. This is planned for a later release.

### Bulk differential expression
- The direct bulk DE tool (`run_bulk_de_direct`) applies an out-group expression filter by default, which is designed for marker genes. On typical bulk data it can remove most genes; if it removes all of them, the tool refuses and says so. For bulk designs, use `run_de_with_formula`. The default will be revised in a later release.

### Custom code
- Custom code (`execute_custom_code`) runs locally with your own user permissions. Enable it only for agents you trust with your workspace.
- The value your code returns as its result may be at most 16 MiB. If it is larger, Lobster reports that the result could not be read and saves no figure from that run. For large outputs, write them to a file in your workspace or store them as a dataset, and return a short summary instead.

### Figures
- Creating the same HTML view twice at the same moment can leave a duplicate view.
- If Lobster cannot remove an old figure revision's file from disk, the file stays in place and keeps using disk space.
- Local figure deletion is not yet available as a CLI command or agent tool.
- The classic terminal plot dashboard does not list figures saved by custom code; the native figure listing does.
_releases.name: Lobster AI v1.2.1

# Lobster AI 1.2.0

## Installation

```bash
uv pip install "lobster-ai[full]==1.2.0"
```

[PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/lobster-ai/1.2.0/) · [Documentation](https://docs.omics-os.com)

## Write checks and read refusals
- Export tools, saves, spills, auto-save, data packages, content caches and queue runs check their destination before the first write. A destination inside the managed figure folder is declined with a fixed message, and nothing is written there.
- If a queue run is stopped after it has started, the reply says that some queue entries may already have been updated.
- Save and auto-save report the datasets that were not saved instead of counting them as saved.
- HDF5 reads that Lobster refuses stay refused; the pandas HDF fallback reader is removed.

## Changes you may notice
- QC drawings now use metrics computed by the quality-analysis step; run `assess_data_quality` first. Drawing no longer adds QC columns to your dataset.
- Programmatic calls to the native visualization tools now require a full LangChain ToolCall (`id`, `name`, `args`). Exported native drawing code calls the services directly and needs no ToolCall.
- The custom-code tool can be switched on or off per agent; see "Custom code" below for the defaults and the switch.
- Custom code: the value your code returns as its result may be at most 16 MiB. If it is larger, Lobster reports that the result could not be read and saves no figure from that run. For large outputs, write them to a file in your workspace or store them as a dataset, and return a short summary instead.
- `lobster scaffold agent` now generates packages pinned to `lobster-ai~=1.2`.
- The direct bulk DE tool refuses with a clear reason when its default expression filter removes every gene, instead of storing an empty result.
- `/plots` counts saved figures and their revisions separately.
- `make dev-install` installs lobster-vector before lobster-metadata.

## Custom code
- Custom code (`execute_custom_code`) runs locally with your own user permissions. Enable it only for agents you trust with your workspace. By default only supervisor, data_expert_agent, metadata_assistant and visualization_expert_agent have it (configurable per agent via `[agent_settings.<agent>]` code_tool in the workspace config.toml or `LOBSTER_CODE_TOOL_<AGENT>`).
  Example: `export LOBSTER_CODE_TOOL_VISUALIZATION_EXPERT_AGENT=0` turns it off for the visualization agent (per-agent values are `1` or `0`; `LOBSTER_CODE_TOOL=all|none|default` sets all agents, and a per-agent value wins). In the workspace `config.toml`:
  ```toml
  [agent_settings.data_expert_agent]
  code_tool = false
  ```

## Known limitations
### Data import
- If saving a required GEO import fails (for example, disk full), that queue entry cannot be retried in the same session, and a partial file may remain in the workspace. Delete it and restart the session.

### Bulk differential expression
- The direct bulk DE tool (`run_bulk_de_direct`) applies an out-group expression filter by default, which is designed for marker genes. On typical bulk data it can remove most genes; if it removes all of them, the tool now refuses and says so. For bulk designs, use `run_de_with_formula`. The default will be revised in a later release.

### Custom code
- The value your code returns as its result may be at most 16 MiB. If it is larger, Lobster reports that the result could not be read and saves no figure from that run. For large outputs, write them to a file in your workspace or store them as a dataset, and return a short summary instead.

### Figures
- Creating the same HTML view twice at the same moment can leave a duplicate view. Nothing is corrupted.
- If removing an old figure revision from disk fails, the file is left in place. Space is leaked conservatively and no data is lost.
- Local figure deletion is not yet available as a CLI command or agent tool.
- The classic terminal plot dashboard does not list figures saved by custom code; the native figure listing does.

### Testing
- One test in a public CI job needs PyTables, which that job's environment does not install. It is a test-fixture issue and is fixed in 1.2.1.

## Changes

**Plots**
- The agent now reports saved plots truthfully. `create_interactive_plot` names the saved workspace-relative path, or says why a file was not written (for example, PNG export skipped because Kaleido 1.0 or later is not installed). It never names an unwritten file.
- `list_workspace_files()` gains a `plots` category, so new plots appear in the artifact manifest after a turn.
- Save failures relayed to the model contain only the description and the file name, never an absolute path.

**Models**
- `LOBSTER_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` is now read as the Bedrock provider default. Before, nothing read it and deployments silently ran the catalog default. `--model`, workspace config and global config still take precedence.
- The `.env` templates no longer document `LOBSTER_<AGENT>_MODEL` and `LOBSTER_GLOBAL_MODEL`, which were never read; they point to the real mechanisms instead.

**Dependencies**
- pandas 3 and numpy 2.5 are supported, and the `pandas<3` and `numpy<2.5` ceilings are removed. The unit, package and notebook replay suites pass under pandas 3.0.6 / numpy 2.5.4 and under pandas 2.3.3.
  - lobster-ml detects text columns correctly under pandas 3; exported notebooks need no Lobster import for this.
  - GWAS LD pruning works under pandas 3.
- Raised minimum versions past known critical/high advisories: lxml 6.1.0, docling 2.94.0, docling-core 2.74.1, python-multipart 0.0.30, transformers 5.10.0 (drug-discovery), sentence-transformers 5.6.0 (vector).
- TUI: golang.org/x/net 0.61.0; the TUI is built with Go 1.26.
- Still capped upstream: pillow <13 (docling packages cap it), setuptools <82 in lobster-genomics (sgkit needs pkg_resources). chromadb has no fixed release yet.

## Upgrade notes
- If you set `LOBSTER_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID`, Lobster now uses that model as the Bedrock default. Unset it to return to the catalog default.
- Environments that pinned pandas below 3 for Lobster can lift that pin.

[PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/lobster-ai/1.1.431/) · [Documentation](https://docs.omics-os.com)


## Changes

**Inference**
- Hosts can now attach an explicit, immutable model binding to a run. Graphs, specialist agents and lazy helpers use only the supplied binding, and a stale binding is refused instead of reused. This is off by default: the local CLI paths are unchanged.
- The optional native Messages and Converse clients now own streaming, cancellation and cleanup. Their SDK checks are lazy (nothing is imported until a model is requested) and use minimum versions only: `anthropic>=1.7.0`, `httpx2>=2.0.0`.
- Bedrock sends an output-token limit only when one is requested. Without one, the model's own maximum applies. Previously a fixed 4096 default applied, or the requested limit was silently dropped.
- A gateway stream that ends before its completion marker now raises `StreamIncomplete` instead of returning a truncated reply as a success. The transport is closed on every exit path.
- Public text is extracted correctly from structured model messages.

**Metadata and sample handling**
- Exact sample identities and metadata types are kept.
- Numeric metadata is parsed from lossless raw tokens. Continuous covariates are kept, and lossy numeric updates are rejected.
- Mixed annotation typing is reported explicitly.
- Metadata reads require HTTPS.

**Tools and security**
- Shell execution runs child processes with a minimal, allowlisted environment.
- Reentrant ontology loading is prevented, and source clients are released.

## Upgrade notes
- `DataExpertAssistant` (and the GEO helpers that build it) now receives its owning `data_manager`, so it can refuse reuse after that owner becomes bound. Custom code that constructs it directly must pass `data_manager`.
- Agent shell commands no longer inherit the parent environment (for example, API keys). They see only PATH, HOME, USER, TMPDIR, locale and an empty PYTHONPATH.
- Bedrock calls without an explicit `max_tokens` are no longer capped at 4096.

## Changes

- **Security:** `lobster-ai` now requires `fsspec>=2026.6.0` (CVE-2026-104851). Upgrade if you install with pip and an older fsspec is present.
- **Notebook export:** the hash cell in exported notebooks is now titled "Export record (hashes)" and states its limits: the hashes are recorded at export, not checked when the notebook runs, and are not tamper evidence or a compliance claim. JSON keys are unchanged.
- **CI:** notebook export fidelity tests now run in CI, and CI fails if the set of tests that ran differs from the expected list.

## Installation

```bash
uv pip install "lobster-ai[full]==1.1.427"
```

The package suite passed exact-version installation on Linux and registry checksum verification.
